paper_diagnosis: Severe salicylate poisoning resistant to conventional management
disease_label_per_paper: Intentional enteric-coated aspirin overdose with severe salicylate poisoning and suspected pharmacobezoar
presentation_summary: 22-year-old woman with depression and prior suicide history presented after intentional ingestion of 500 enteric-coated 325 mg aspirin tablets about 5 hours before arrival.
She complained of epigastric discomfort and nausea; initial examination showed GCS 12, sinus tachycardia, normal oxygen saturation, and no focal abnormalities.
Admission salicylate concentration was 97.5 mg/dL with compensated metabolic acidosis and normal renal function.
Urinary alkalinization, activated charcoal, and emergent hemodialysis were started, but salicylate levels remained elevated, prompting abdominal radiography that suggested an aspirin pharmacobezoar.

Endoscopy the following day showed gastritis without a visible bezoar; with prolonged hemodialysis, urine alkalinization, and repeated activated charcoal, salicylate levels declined and she was discharged to inpatient psychiatry.
